subject: Pacifica Health — renewal escalation: concession request (SLA addendum + term reset)
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@pacifica.health>
Cc: Pacifica Procurement <procurement@pacifica.health>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 09:25:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal concern — request for SLA addendum and term reset

Hi Liam,

Thanks again for the time last week — appreciate the candid conversation about usage spikes and the impact on your ops teams. As we discussed, your renewal is coming up (RDW-5467) and Pacifica has flagged two items that are blocking signature: a tighter SLA for latency during peak windows, and a request to move the contract to annual billing with a term-reset to zero out the prior partial period (they want alignment with calendar-year budget).

Attached are a proposed SLA addendum (Pacifica_SLA_addendum_draft.pdf) and the mutual action plan (Pacifica_Mutual_Action_Plan_2026.xlsx) that reflects the timeline we discussed. To keep the renewal moving I wanted to be upfront about the concession we can take to the execs: currently looking at a one-time customer credit plus an SLA credit (service-time carveout) if we add the addendum and they sign a 12-month term.

Can you confirm the following from your side:
- If Pacifica signs the SLA addendum, is a 12-month reset acceptable?
- Is the procurement team able to accept a one-time credit in lieu of a recurring discount?

If you confirm, I'll escalate internally for approval — I anticipate needing an exec signoff for any combined concession (credit + nonstandard term reset + SLA attachment). Suggested internal ask: one-time credit of up to 8% of annual committed spend + SLA addendum as drafted.

Propose a quick 30-min call tomorrow if that helps.

Best,
Sooj
--
Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Strategic Renewals
Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@pacifica.health>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Pacifica Procurement <procurement@pacifica.health>
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 13:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal concern — request for SLA addendum and term reset

Sooj, thanks for the note and the drafts. Procurement reviewed and we have two asks before we can sign:

1) Pacifica needs a guaranteed SLA for 99.8% availability during our defined clinical windows; the proposed addendum looks promising but would like the credit to be proportional to outages — we are asking for a 15% one-time credit applied to the first invoice after renewal.
2) Regarding the term-reset, we are pushing to align the renewal to our fiscal year. If Redwood cannot provide a full term reset we will need a 10% recurring discount for the first 6 months to justify the move.

We prefer the one-time credit if possible, but the numbers you're suggesting are still below what our CFO expects. Liam

--
Liam O'Connor
Director, Cloud Ops
Pacifica Health
liam.oconnor@pacifica.health | +1 (206) 555-0133
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Pacifica Procurement <procurement@pacifica.health>
Date: Wed, 2 Sep 2026 10:00:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Renewal concern — request for SLA addendum and term reset

David / Marissa — looping you both in to escalate. Pacifica is pushing for more (see reply below).

Quick summary: customer will sign SLA addendum if we provide either (A) one-time 15% credit (what they asked) or (B) 10% recurring for first 6 months if we won't reset the term fully. Their preference is option A. Current internal position I can commit without exec signoff is up to 5% one-time credit + the SLA addendum as drafted. Anything beyond that needs deal desk / exec approval.

Why this is strategic: Pacifica is a good reference in the healthcare vertical (low churn risk otherwise), and if we give the one-time credit + term reset we keep ARR intact and avoid compounding discounts.

Ask: David — can you authorize escalation to finance/legal for a one-time concession up to 10%? If not, what's the max you can approve so I know whether to push for the 5% internal or request formal exec approval?

Adding the attached MAP for timeline.

Thanks,
Sooj
--
Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Strategic Renewals
Redwood Inference
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Pacifica Procurement <procurement@pacifica.health>
Date: Wed, 2 Sep 2026 15:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal concern — request for SLA addendum and term reset

Team — thanks for the context. I reviewed Pacifica's usage profile and churn risk; I agree this is worth an exception but with guardrails.

Proposal for Exec approval request:
- Concession: one-time credit of 9% of committed annual spend (applied to first invoice after renewal)
- Nonstandard term: reset to a 12-month annual term effective on their renewal date (no retroactive credit beyond the one-time concession)
- SLA: include addendum as drafted; we will add a clause capping cumulative credits from SLA breaches to the one-time 9% to limit future exposure
- Revenue protection: a minimum revenue commitment for the first 6 months post-renewal (if they under-consume by >40%, we resume standard billing)

If leadership signs off on the 9% one-time credit + SLA addendum and term reset, legal should prepare an addendum + DocuSign link. Finance needs to confirm the accounting treatment (offset vs credit) — I will loop in billing.

Next step: Marissa, please present this package to Hannah for sign-off. If Hannah approves at the 9% level, I'll get legal and finance to prepare paperwork. If not, bring back with the counter delta.

-David
--
David Kim
VP, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Pacifica Procurement <procurement@pacifica.health>
Date: Thu, 3 Sep 2026 17:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal concern — request for SLA addendum and term reset

Marissa / David / Sooj — I reviewed the ask and supporting rationale. Approve the following (final exec decision):

- One-time customer credit of 8% of the committed annual contract value.
- Term reset to a 12-month annual term as requested, effective on renewal signature.
- SLA addendum to be included as drafted; include David's cap (cumulative credits limited to the one-time 8%).
- Requirement: Pacifica must sign the SLA addendum and the mutual action plan within 10 business days and confirm billing alignment; DocuSign link to be sent by Legal.

Finance: apply as a one-time invoice credit on the first renewal invoice (do not amortize). Legal: prepare the addendum and DocuSign envelope; include the revenue protection language David suggested. Ops: flag for post-signature monitoring.

Sooj — communicate the approved package to Liam and procurement, attach the SLA addendum, and get the signed MAP back. Copy me on final execution.

Hannah
